body:
In the hope of getting more contributors, I'm going to leave my diagnosis of the bug up here for a little while before I take a pass at fixing it.

The specific problem in this bug is that we don't add cookies on a prepared request to the Session unless they were set by the server. There are three possible scopes for this fix:
1. Only fix up the occurrences of this bug in the top-level functions, e.g `requests.request()`. This _must_ be fixed, because otherwise cookies are stupid for these functions. The logic behind this restriction is that if you want cookies on all requests in a session, you should set them on the `Session` object.
2. Add all cookies set through the functional API to the correct `Session` object. It's not entirely clear that this is the right thing to do: these cookies should probably have been set on the `Session`.
3. Do something 'magic' for redirects.

As for the super-extra bonus bug, the offending lines of code are these in `SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects()`:

``` python
headers = prepared_request.headers
try:
    del headers['Cookie']
except KeyError:
    pass
```

combined with the implementation of `PreparedRequest.copy()`:

``` python
def copy(self):
    p = PreparedRequest()
    p.method = self.method
    p.url = self.url
    p.headers = self.headers
    p.body = self.body
    p.hooks = self.hooks
    return p
```

Nice little teachable lesson about python's mutable data structures right there.

issue.title: Problem with missing cookies after redirect

repository.name: requests
repository.description: A simple, yet elegant, HTTP library.

issue.body:
I sent this by e-mail - no response. I think this might be of interest to others:

> I have a problem when connecting to a site. Here's the scenario:
> 
> 1) I enter a login page, which has a form
> 2) I send (using Requests) a POST with the username, pw, etc.
>    (This POST includes the SESSIONID)
> 3) The webpage with a 302,
> 4) To which requests does automatically a GET to the new address
> 5) In Firefox, this works, In Requests, I get redirected to the
>    login - page (with another 302).
> 
> The only important difference I can detect is that in point 4),
> Firefox repeats automatically the SESSION ID, which Requests does
> not do. Can I enable this?

I solved the problem by disabling automatic redirects, and creating
a new request manually, with the sessionid cookie. Now the process
runs successfully. 

This confirms the necessity of the repeating the cookie in the 
request after the 302, but it defeat the 'neatness' of the auto
redirects.

Cheers,
John

body:
@Lukasa I will try on it.
I think implementing deepcopy of models.PreparedRequest and call req.deepcopy() instead of req.copy() will fix super extra bonus bug easily. Is there any expectable drawback of using deepcopy?
@daftshady It's unnecessary. =) `PreparedRequest.copy()` should just make sure it calls `req.headers.copy()` to get the new head dict. =)

@Lukasa It' s strange.. I think even if PreparedRequest.copy creates new object, as you know,  assignment like this (p.headers = self.headers) only make shallow copy of CaseInsensitiveDict. so the change in new `p` created by copy() can affect origin so that extra bonus bug happens.
Anyway, i will try another way to fix it if you think deepcopy is not suitable =)

Assignment like that does not make a shallow copy. =) It doesn't make a copy at all, instead both names point to the same object. That's why `CaseInsensitiveDict.copy()` is enough: it returns a new object which is a shallow copy of the original dictionary.

To try to clear this up, observe the following:

``` python
# Create two dictionaries.
>>> a = {'first': 'dict'}
>>> b = {'second': 'dict'}

# Assign C to A using equals, create D using copy().
>>> c = a
>>> d = b.copy()

# Observe that A and C are the same objects, while B and D are not.
>>> a is c
True
>>> b is d
False

# This means that any change that affects A will also affect C. This is our bonus bug.
>>> a['third'] = 'value'
>>> a
{'third': 'value', 'first': 'dict'}
>>> c
{'third': 'value', 'first': 'dict'}

# But changes that affect B do not affect D.
>>> b['fourth'] = 'value'
>>> b
{'second': 'dict', 'fourth': 'value'
>>> d
{'second': 'dict'}
```

@Lukasa I understand. I misunderstood that you are saying 'p.headers = self.headers' is just enough.
As you said, `CaseInsensitiveDict.copy()` works correctly. So just fixing it to 'p.headers = self.headers.copy() is enough, not deepcopy.

In your example, if

> > > b = {'first' : [1,2,3]}
> > > d = b.copy()
> > > b is d
> > > False
> > > b['first'].append(4)
> > > b
> > > {'first' : [1,2,3,4]}
> > > d
> > > {'first' : [1,2,3,4]}
> > > Changes that affect B can affect D in this case.

But, as you said, `CaseInsensitiveDict.copy()` is just enough to fix extra bonus bug.
Sorry for my carelessness =)
Not a problem. =D Glad we're on the same page.

issue.title: Request cookies should not be persisted to session

repository.name: requests
repository.description: A simple, yet elegant, HTTP library.

issue.body:
After the fix for #1630, cookies sent with a request are now incorrectly persisted to the session.

Specifically, problem lies here: https://github.com/kennethreitz/requests/blob/1511dfa637643bae5b6111a20ecb80ec9ae26032/requests/sessions.py#L330

Removing that breaks the test case for #1630 though, still investigating a solution.
